full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J:- The Judgment of reversal has been called in question by invoking the revisional Jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court on laying an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff against the judgment and decree dated 11-11-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Tangail allowing the Appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 23-9-1998 and 29-9-1998 respectively passed in Other Class Suit No. 8 of 1997 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem tit and proper 

 18. The learned Advocate for the petitioner lastly submits that the judgment of the trial Judge is ambiguous, perverse but the Judgment of the trial Judge is very much well reasoned judgment as such the judgment of the trial Judge does not suffer from any legal infirmity, perversity and material irregularity for which the very reversal of the last court of fact under its Appellate Jurisdiction was not proper and not in accordance with law and the same is liable to beset aside. 

 21. The final Court of fact at the time of disposal of the appeal did not at all consider the aforesaid averments of the PWs who categorically was able to prove .the case of the plaintiffs, In order to reverse the findings of the trial Judge the last court of fact must reverse the finding specifically and must show that such findings of the trial Judge were perverse not in accordance with law, based on total non consideration of evidence which resulted in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice but as a matter of fact the final Court of fact did not follow the principles as laid down in Section 115 of the Code of Civil. Procedure at the time of reversal of the findings of the trial Judge the aforesaid principle has been well settled in the case of Nurul Abser Chowdhury Vs. Jesmin Akhter reported in 51 DLR P-352. The same principle of law has also been followed in the case of Waliullah Vs. Hasina Begum and others reported in 23 BLD(HCD)( 2003) page-67. 

 22. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Judge I find that the trial Judge arrived its finding on due and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record and rightly arrived at its finding on due consideration of the exhibits which on appeal the last court of fact arrived its finding on very perfunctory manner and according to me the said finding of the appellate Court is based on serious miscarriage of justice, perversity and not a proper judgment of reversal. I also find the appellate court in passing the impugned judgment has totally misconceived, misdirected in arriving its finding. The final court of fact passed the impugned judgment and decree in violation of the mandatory provisions of law as contained in section 115 of the Code of .Civil Procedure and also in violation of the provisions of law as contained in Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I also find the impugned Judgment and decree of the final court of fact is not a proper judgment of reversal and the same has suffered' from serious miscarriage of justice. I also find the last court of fact failed to give its reasoning’s on due consideration of the materials on record and arrived at its own independent findings on the issues involved in the case while reversing the decision of the trial Judge in violation of the settled principles of law as laid down in the case of Md. Ibrahim Vs. Md. Alauddin and others reported in 27 DLR page 413 and also in the case of Rostom Ali Dhakua being dead his heirs Rustom ali Dhakua and others Vs. Abdur Rahman dead his heirs Razia Khatun and others reported in 14 BLD (AD)(1994) page- 229 where it is clearly held that "affirming the decision of the trial court must independently consider the evidence on record. But in the case of "affirming the findings of the trial court the narration of the entire evidence and reiteration of the reasons given by the trial court are not essential. In such a case expressions of general agreement with those of the trial court are generally considered sufficient. But in the case of a reversal of the judgment, the consideration of the evidence of necessity has to be through and more elaborate." On record here in the instant case the final court of fact at the time of reversal of the judgment of the trial court failed to assess and consider the evidence on record independently as such the impugned judgment and decree of the last court of fact is not a proper judgment in accordance with law. In view of the submissions citations and the attending circumstances of the case. I have no hesitation to reverse the judgment and decree of the last court of fact as the same has suffered from serious miscarriage of justice. The citations as referred by the learned Advocate in support of his contentions are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
